text: Code refactoring is the process of improving the structure of existing code without changing what it does. The main goal is to make the code easier to read, understand, and maintain. For example, you might rename unclear variables, break a long function into smaller ones, or remove repeated logic. These changes do not add new features or fix bugs; the program should behave exactly the same after refactoring. Refactoring also helps reduce technical debt, which builds up when code is written quickly and becomes messy over time. Although it takes extra effort, regular refactoring keeps a project healthy and saves time in the future.
